'''Henning Scheich''' (12 May 1942 – 30 May 2025) was a German brain researcher and psychiatrist. He was director of the [[Leibniz Institute for Neurobiology]] until 2010 and head of the institute department until 2013. 

== Life and career ==
[[File:Jamming Avoidance Response Eigenmannia.png|thumb|300px| Two neighboring ''[[Eigenmannia]]'' perform the [[Jamming avoidance response]]. When a fish with an electric discharge of 400 Hz encounters another fish with the same discharge frequency, one fish shifts its frequency upward and the other shifts its frequency downward.]]
After finishing school at the Geschwister-Scholl-Gymnasium in Düsseldorf, Scheich studied medicine and philosophy at the [[University of Cologne]] from 1961 to 1963, at [[LMU Munich]] from 1963 to 1964 and from 1965 to 1966, and at the [[University of Montpellier]], France, from 1964 to 1965. He concluded his medicine studies with the [[State examination]] at LMU Munich in 1966.
From 1967 to 1969, Scheich worked as a PhD student on the human [[Electroencephalography|electroencephalogram (EEG)]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Psychiatry]] Munich in the department run by [[Otto Detlev Creutzfeldt]]. He completed his PhD degree ''with highest praise'' (''summa cum laude'') in 1969. While working on his PhD, he published a series of scientific works on the physiology of the visual system of cats.<ref name= vit>{{cite web |url= http://www.cbbs.eu/images/pdf/Scheich_CV_cs.pdf | title=Prof. Dr. med. Henning Scheich  |publisher=center for behavioral brain sciences  | date=  | author= | accessdate= 3 July 2020}}</ref>

From 1969 to 1972, Scheich served as post-doctoral student under [[Theodore H. Bullock]] at the [[University of California, San Diego]], USA. Here he participated in the research on the [[Jamming avoidance response]], a characteristic of [[Behavioral communication]] among [[electric fish]] and on its neurophysiological foundations. From 1972 to 1974, Scheich led a research group at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]], Göttingen, on the subject of ''acoustic communication''.<ref>{{cite journal |url= https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.185.4148.365 | title=Neuronal Analysis of Wave Form in the Time Domain: Midbrain Units in Electric Fish during Social Behavior  |publisher=center for behavioral brain sciences  | date=26 July 1974 | author=Henning Scheich | journal=Science | volume=185 | issue=4148 | pages=365–367 | doi=10.1126/science.185.4148.365 | pmid=4834368 | bibcode=1974Sci...185..365S | s2cid=35922801 | accessdate= 3 July 2020| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1974, Scheich accepted a professorship for zoology  and neurobiology at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]]. Between 1977 and 1985, he undertook field research trips to the [[Amazon basin]], Central Africa and Thailand, where he studied electric fish and the [[Behavioral communication]] of birds, that led to the discovery of [[Ultrasonic hearing]]. Scheich was guest professor at the [[Ponce Health Sciences University]] in Puerto Rico and joined the [[Australian National University]] in Canberra, for a research period, during which time he discovered the electric sensory organ of the [[platypus]].<ref name="Information1988">{{cite book|title=New Scientist|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nfJPdScNqJsC&pg=PA39|date=12 May 1988|publisher=Reed Business Information|pages=39–}}</ref><ref name= vit/>

After German reunification and the foundation of the [[Leibniz Association|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Science Association]] in 1992, Scheich was appointed director and head of the department at the [[Leibniz Institute for Neurobiology]] (IfN, since 2010 LIN) in [[Magdeburg]], that included a professorship for physiology at the medical faculty of the [[Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg]]. The LIN, that has originated from an institute of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|Scientific Academy of the GDR]] (East Germany), focuses on research into the mechanisms of learning and memory. The research program of Scheich at the LIN concentrated on the organisation of auditory and vocal behaviour in animals and humans and in this context on the role of the [[Auditory cortex]] during learning events. In 2003 Scheich participated in the establishment of the annual ''International Conference on Auditory Cortex'' event.<ref name="HeilScheich2005">{{cite book|author=Peter Heil, Henning Scheich, Eike Budinger, Reinhard Konig|title=The Auditory Cortex: A Synthesis of Human and Animal Research|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=F4J5AgAAQBAJ&pg=PR7|date=6 May 2005|publisher=Psychology Press|isbn=978-1-135-61336-5|pages=7–}}</ref>
Scheich's tenure as the director of the LIN ended in 2010. During the same year he also retired from the Otto-von-Guericke University. From 2014 to 2018 Scheich has continued his work with his emeritus group.<ref name= vit/>

Scheich missed no opportunity to publicly emphasize the significance of brain research for human education and was involved in organisations associated with research support, the self-administration of science and political counselling (e.g. the so-called 'Blue List' Committee, the Evaluation Committee of the German Council of Science and Humanities, the Heisenberg Committee of the German Research Foundation, the Health Research Council of the [[Federal Ministry of Education and Research (Germany)|Federal Ministry of Education and Research]]).<ref name= vit/><ref name="Becker2006">{{cite book|author=Nicole Becker|title=Die neurowissenschaftliche Herausforderung der Pädagogik|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WEYehvhzJ4oC&pg=PA89|year=2006|publisher=Julius Klinkhardt|isbn=978-3-7815-1436-2|pages=89–}}</ref>

Scheich died on 30 May 2025, at the age of 83.<ref>Constanze Seidenbecher: [https://www.lin-magdeburg.de/institut/oeffentlichkeitsarbeit/news/beitrag/zum-tod-von-prof-dr-henning-scheich Zum Tod von Prof. Dr. Henning Scheich]. lin-magdeburg.de, 6 June 2025 (in German). Retrieved 9 June 2025.</ref>

== Honours and memberships ==
* 1995 to 2003 – Vice president of the [[Leibniz Association|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Science Association]]
* 2000 – [[Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]
* 2007 – [[Order of Merit of Saxony-Anhalt]]
* 2013 – Golden Book of the City of Magdeburg<ref name =buch>{{cite web |url= http://magdeburgpost.de/index.php/rubriken/politik/itemlist/tag/Goldenes%20Buch | title=Prof. Dr. Ernst Dieter Gilles und Prof. Dr. Henning Scheich trugen sich in das Goldene Buch der Landeshauptstadt Magdeburg ein Gründungsdirektoren des Max-Planck- und Leibniz-Instituts zu Gast im Rathaus    |publisher=Magdeburg Post  | date= 4 July 2013 | author= | accessdate= 3 July 2020}}</ref>
